title: Side-panel rollout: keystroke-first a11y & i18n prototype review
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Deliver a keyboard-first side-panel UI for rollout controls that meets WCAG AA contrast and screen-reader announceability across locales (including RTL). This ticket covers the prototype review, accessibility acceptance criteria, and a lightweight i18n readiness pass.

Scope: the side-panel that appears on the right when a rollout is selected in Dashboards -> Rollouts. Focus areas: predictable focus order inside the panel, explicit focus return to the originating list item, ARIA live announcements for variant changes, concise microcopy that localizes cleanly, and color-token mappings that meet contrast when token substitutions occur.

Acceptance criteria:
- Keyboard-only users can open the panel, navigate all controls in a linear and discoverable order, and close the panel returning focus to the launching element.
- All interactive elements meet 4.5:1 contrast at default scale; decorative tokens tested at 3:1 where applicable with accessible text alternatives.
- Screen readers hear a brief, non-redundant live announcement when the rollout variant changes and when a canary rollout enters a degraded state. Announcement phrasing is locale-ready and avoids concatenating untranslated fragments.
- UI strings account for pluralization and length expansion (+30% in longer languages). Layout tolerances documented in the Figma prototype.
- RTL behavior verified for ordering and focus traps; focus ring visuals flip correctly and do not overlap clipped content.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Pattern chosen: side-panel vs inline drawer. Side-panel preserves timeline context and reduces DOM churn for long lists but requires explicit focus-return handling.
- We propose a single ARIA live region for variant state updates (polled writes) rather than per-control announcements to reduce verbosity; accessibility review flagged this as acceptable provided message aggregation and deduplication rules are enforced.
- Color tokens use semantic names (accent-critical, neutral-foreground) to allow runtime color-scheme swaps (dark/light and high-contrast). We accept a minor visual delta vs the current mockups in exchange for consistent token mapping across products.

Artifacts and links:
- Figma prototype (side-panel flows): https://www.figma.com/file/REDACTED/console-rollouts-sidepanel-proto
- Confluence spec (focus behavior + ARIA examples): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CONSOLE/pages/REDACTED/Sidepanel+Rollout+a11y+Spec
- GitHub branch/PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/REDACTED
- Usability test notes and recordings: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/REDACTED

Measurement plan:
- Run a 5-person keyboard-only usability pass (mix of engineers and TPMs) and document time-to-task and discovered blockers.
- Run Lighthouse a11y checks and axe-core automated scans on the prototype; record issues and triage into ENG backlog.
- Run visual contrast checks with token swapped palettes (dark, light, high-contrast).

Next steps:
1) Incorporate PM microcopy suggestions (see comment thread) and hand off final tokens to ENG for dev spike.
2) Engineering to implement focus-return utility and one ARIA live region per rollout panel.
3) Localization team to review strings for pluralization and contextual placeholders before UX sign-off.
4) QA to run keyboard and screen-reader checklist (see attachments).
comments: 2026-03-01 Maya Chen: Created ticket after initial design spike. Attached first-pass Figma with two patterns (inline drawer, side-panel). Asked ENG to evaluate focus-return feasibility.

2026-03-03 Jonah Patel: PM review — prefers side-panel for visibility of timeline. Asked to confirm microcopy for canary/degraded states to avoid alarmist wording for customers during expected rollouts.

2026-03-04 Accessibility review (L. Ortiz): Live-region aggregation OK if messages are de-duped and include status context. Confirmed 4.5:1 requirement for interactive text; recommended contrast token fallback list.

2026-03-06 Eng sync (A. Kumar): Feasibility OK. Proposed focus-return util that stores the element id on open and restores on close; noted edge-case for virtualized lists — will coordinate with ENG-88421.
2026-03-07 Localization review (S. Müller): Flagged two microcopy strings that use English word order which will break in Arabic/Hebrew. Requested placeholders and sentence templates for translators.
2026-03-09 Design update: Updated Figma with pluralization tokens and layout padding expansion to handle +30% string growth. Requested follow-up on color token mapping for high-contrast mode.
2026-03-10 Jonah Patel: Marked In Review and requested keyboard-only QA pass next week. Assigned QA checklist to @QA team lead in comment thread.
